title: Implement privacy review requirements for onboarding telemetry (allowlist, redaction, retention tags)
creator: Nadia Rahman
description:
## Context
Security/Legal completed the privacy & security review for Guided Onboarding telemetry. We are approved to proceed to beta/GA **only if** we implement the MUST requirements.

This ticket covers implementation changes required across:
- Console Web telemetry emission (guardrails against disallowed properties)
- Telemetry ingestion validation (property allowlist + drop unknown)
- Redaction/drop rules for known dangerous keys (prompt/messages/completion/auth headers/etc.)
- Retention tagging and storage config for raw onboarding events (30d) vs aggregated datasets (13mo)

Refs:
- Confluence: Onboarding telemetry privacy & security review (Hosted API guided onboarding) — v1 (created 2026-02-14, updated 2026-02-22)
- Confluence: Onboarding Telemetry Event Schema v1 (Guided Onboarding Checklist) (updated 2026-02-21)

## Problem
Current instrumentation work (ENG-23112 / PRs in flight) emits onboarding events but does not yet enforce privacy constraints end-to-end. Without hard guardrails we risk accidentally collecting customer content (prompt/messages), secrets (API keys/tokens), full URLs with querystrings, or free-form error messages.

## Goals
1) Enforce strict allowlisting at ingestion for the onboarding telemetry stream.
2) Ensure disallowed keys are dropped/redacted even if accidentally attached by a producer.
3) Apply retention tags/TTL so raw events expire at 30 days; aggregated datasets use longer retention.
4) Ensure URL hygiene: strip query params except allowlisted UTM params; store docs reference as stable identifier or path only.
5) Provide tests + monitoring so regressions are caught quickly during beta.

## Non-goals
- Reworking product analytics beyond onboarding stream
- Building org-level deletion tooling beyond existing retention window mechanisms (handled by platform processes)
- Changing the schema itself (v1); this ticket implements enforcement

## Implementation plan
### A) Ingestion allowlist + schema enforcement (MUST)
- Add onboarding stream configuration: `schema_context=guided_onboarding_checklist` with an explicit property allowlist.
- Drop any property not in the allowlist.
- Reject events with oversized payloads.
- Enforce enumerated values for:
  - `source` (console_web|console_backend)
  - `environment` (prod|staging)
- Enforce that `event_name` is one of the v1 onboarding events.

Deliverable: merged change in telemetry-ingest / pipeline config and rollout to all regions.

### B) Redaction/drop rules for dangerous keys (MUST)
Even with allowlisting, producers may send nested objects or error payloads. Add an explicit denylist scan before allowlist projection:
- Drop (or hard-fail) if any of these keys exist anywhere in the payload (top-level or nested):
  - `prompt`, `messages`, `completion`, `tool_arguments`, `function_call`, `embeddings`, `request_body`, `response_body`, `headers`, `authorization`, `cookie`, `api_key`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`
- Drop any value that looks like a bearer token pattern if it appears in an allowed field (defense-in-depth). If detected, replace with `[REDACTED]` and emit a pipeline metric `onboarding_telemetry_redaction_count`.

Open question to resolve in review: do we prefer *hard-fail & quarantine* vs *best-effort redaction* for token-like values in allowed string fields?

### C) Retention tags / TTL config (MUST)
- Raw onboarding telemetry events: 30 day TTL (region-local).
- Telemetry health metrics: 90 days.
- Aggregated onboarding funnel tables: 13 months (no per-actor rows).

Deliverable: storage policy config changes + confirmation in US + EU that raw tables are not replicated cross-region.

### D) Producer-side guardrails (MUST)
Console Web:
- Ensure onboarding telemetry helper only accepts a typed payload and performs an allowlist pick before sending.
- Do not attach `Error` objects, stack traces, or raw exception messages.
- Ensure docs click event stores path only / stable doc id. Strip query params except `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_content`.

Console Backend:
- Ensure validators emit only enumerated `error_code` and never serialize raw exception text.
- Ensure `dedupe_key` does not contain unbounded/high-entropy content.

### E) Tests (MUST)
- Unit tests for ingestion allowlist: unknown keys dropped.
- Unit tests for denylist scan: payload containing `messages` / `prompt` is rejected/quarantined.
- Tests for URL sanitization.
- Canary test event in staging that verifies retention tags are applied.

### F) Monitoring & alerting (SHOULD)
- Metric + alert for `unknown_property_dropped_count` spikes.
- Metric + alert for `redaction_count` spikes.
- Dashboard panel confirming raw events TTL job is running.

## Acceptance criteria
- Raw onboarding telemetry tables in prod have 30-day retention and do not replicate EU raw data out of region.
- Ingestion allowlist is enforced for onboarding stream; unknown props are dropped.
- Denylisted keys are blocked from storage (no occurrences in raw tables during beta verification).
- Console docs link telemetry stores path only (no querystrings beyond UTM allowlist).
- Security reviewer (Marcus Lin) signs off that MUST items from the privacy review are satisfied.

## Rollout / risk
- Rollout ingestion enforcement behind a stream-config flag in staging first; then prod US; then EU/APAC.
- Expect some event volume drop due to stricter validation; coordinate with ENG-23119 dashboards so we can distinguish "dropped" vs "missing".

## Notes
This is a gating item for expanding beta cohort (see ENG-23118 rollout).
comments: 2026-02-18 (Nadia Rahman): Creating this as the enforcement follow-up from the privacy review. We need hard barriers at ingestion + producer helpers so we can confidently say we never collect prompt content, even accidentally.

2026-02-19 (Marcus Lin): +1. MUST: denylist scan for `prompt/messages/completion/authorization/api_key` (including nested). Also confirm no full URLs w/ query strings are stored. Prefer hard-fail/quarantine over silent redaction for disallowed keys so we notice regressions.

2026-02-20 (Dylan Brooks): Confirming scope: Console Web helper changes + backend validator sanitization are doable in this cycle. Ingestion config will be owned by Nadia/Telemetry pipeline folks but we can implement and test from Console side. Hannah can take point on producer changes.

2026-02-21 (Hannah Rivera): I can implement a `trackOnboardingEvent()` wrapper that (1) picks from an allowlist per event_name, (2) sanitizes doc URLs, (3) blocks if it sees disallowed keys. Question: do we want client-side block (don’t send) or send-to-ingest and let ingest quarantine? My preference: block in client + ingest enforcement as backstop.
2026-02-22 (Michael Grant): Legal note: avoid capturing free-form error strings. Enumerated categories only. Also, do not store any truncated/hashed prompt content. Hard prohibition.

2026-02-24 (Nadia Rahman): Drafted ingestion rules: (a) denylist scan then (b) allowlist projection. We’ll emit `ingest_drop_reason` metric labels but not store the original payload when dropped. Working with Logan to confirm quarantine location for debugging is security-only.

2026-02-26 (Marcus Lin): Quarantine can exist but must be access-controlled and still not retain content-bearing payloads. If denylist triggers, safest is to drop without storing the body and rely on metrics/alerts + request_id correlation.

2026-03-01 (Hannah Rivera): Implemented URL sanitizer for docs clicks: strips host, strips query params except UTM allowlist, and converts known docs URLs to `docs_url_id` where available. Also removed any `error.message` attachments in onboarding events.

2026-03-04 (Nadia Rahman): Ingestion allowlist now deployed to staging. Seeing ~3% drop due to unknown keys from `onboarding.checklist_viewed` (field name mismatch: `checklistVariant` vs `checklist_variant`). Hannah to align Console emitter to schema naming; then we can roll to prod.
activity: 2026-03-04: Status updated to In Progress; staging ingestion enforcement enabled
